articles.headline: Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'
articles.description: Bronny James said he hasn't spoken much to his father, LeBron, about the decision to leave the Lakers this summer, but said he's excited to face him on Christmas.
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- When LeBron James left the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son and teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So, it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path, and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself, and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So, he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history. Whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father-and-son duo entered the game together or last season in the playoffs, when they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. Navigating a complex free agency where the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books.

Bronny James, whose $2.3 million contract for this season is guaranteed, said that he has spent the summer focusing on his role backing up Lakers guards Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. Bronny played in 42 games last season and eight playoff games.

"You guys know me as Bronny. My real name is LeBron. I've been doing this for however long," Bronny James said. "It's a motivating factor for me just getting up every day and trying to prove myself as Bronny instead of LeBron."

Though LeBron and Bronny might not have spoken about the move much, Bronny wishes his father well and is looking forward to the first time the Lakers face the 76ers this season, on Christmas in L.A.

"I'm happy for him and excited to see where their season goes," Bronny James said. "I'm excited to see him on Christmas. I'm excited to play against him on Christmas, so that's going to be good."

Not having LeBron is a significant adjustment for the Lakers and his son. L.A. has nine new players and is trying to focus on this season and not on the past. It is the start of the first season without LeBron since 2017-18.

"It was kind of sad [that he left]; playing with LeBron was amazing," Doncic said about James' departure. "There's a lot of things I learned from him, and we all know who LeBron James is. We spent time together, and it was amazing."

articles.headline: Seahawks' Mike Macdonald says team still believes in RB Jadarian Price
articles.description: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald says the team has not lost faith in starting running back Jadarian Price after the rookie first-round pick lost a fumble for the second week in a row on Sunday.
articles.body:
SEATTLE -- Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald says the team has not lost faith in starting running back Jadarian Price after the rookie first-round pick lost a fumble for the second week in a row on Sunday.

"With JD, he understands what's going on," Macdonald said Monday. "He needs to take care of the ball. I think there's some things fundamentally where we can focus on. We're going to continue to give him the ball. We trust him and we know he's going to work really hard to do his part as well."

Price's lost fumble in the first quarter on Sunday gave the Washington Commanders a short field, setting up their first touchdown. It was one of three turnovers the Seahawks committed in a 33-31 loss that snapped their franchise-record 12-game winning streak.

When Price lost a fumble a week earlier in a win over the Arizona Cardinals, the Seahawks went right back to him on the first play of their next drive. But they didn't show the same patience Sunday. After Price's fumble at the 11:06 mark of the first quarter, his next carry wasn't until the 12:49 mark of the third quarter, though he was targeted twice in that span.

Price finished with five carries for 15 yards, plus one catch for 7 yards. Despite making his third straight start, he played 19 of Seattle's 67 offensive snaps, while Emanuel Wilson (nine carries for 14 yards) and George Holani (eight touches for 58 yards) each played 24 snaps.

"I think just as a team, if we turn the ball over, it's not good business," Macdonald said postgame. "I know he didn't come back after the initial fumble. We decided to calm it down and bring him back after the half, but he's going to be fine. He's going to figure it out. He'll be fine."

Price fumbled five times over three seasons as a backup at Notre Dame.

The Seahawks, meanwhile, have not dealt with this problem in recent years. Ken Walker III -- whom Price was drafted to replace -- fumbled only three times over four seasons with Seattle but did not lose any of them. Zach Charbonnet - who co-started in 2025 alongside Walker -- did not fumble over his first three seasons.

Drafted 32nd overall, Price has 119 yards on 28 attempts (4.3 average) over three games, plus four catches for 21 yards. He has yet to score an NFL touchdown.

"JD is such a great, great dude," quarterback Sam Darnold said postgame. "And he knows his responsibility. He knows not to turn the ball over, so there's not much you say to him. You just tell him, 'Keep going, and we've got your back.'"

Macdonald said the Seahawks will decide by Tuesday whether to open Charbonnet's 21-day practice window this week. Charbonnet is on the Physically Unable to Perform list following February ACL surgery. He has to spend at least one more game on PUP, but he's been eligible to begin practicing as of last week.

articles.headline: McVay, Rams won't make excuses after pass interference call
articles.description: A day after his team's 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos, Los Angeles coach Sean McVay said the 1-2 Rams will not "play the victim card" because of a debatable defensive pass interference late on cornerback Josh Wallace.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- After rewatching the play on which his team was called for defensive pass interference late in a Week 3 loss to the Denver Broncos, Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay said the Rams will not "play the victim card" because of the call.

The play came on third-and-6 from the Los Angeles 11, when cornerback Josh Wallace intercepted a pass by Broncos quarterback Bo Nix. Wallace was called for defensive pass interference on Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant, giving Denver first-and-goal at the Rams' 7. The Broncos scored on the drive to take a 30-26 lead with 47 seconds left.

"[It] doesn't really matter," McVay said Monday. "It is what it is. That was the call that was made and there was a lot of opportunities that we had to be able to close the door on that game. ... But I wouldn't have any additional coaching points for how Josh [Wallace] plays through the cycle of the snap. But I'm not going to make excuses either and we're not going to play the victim card."

The Rams were called for five penalties in the final two minutes of the fourth quarter, tied for the most by any team in a game since 2000, according to ESPN Research. Referee Bill Vinovich's crew had thrown the second-fewest flags in the final two minutes of a game in the 2024 and '25 seasons. The group threw only one flag in the last two minutes across the entire 2024 season.

The Rams ended that game without cornerback Jaylen Watson, who dislocated his arm late in the second quarter. McVay said Watson has dealt with that injury before and although Watson probably will not play in Week 4 against the Eagles, the Rams don't plan to put the cornerback on injured reserve.

Tight end Terrance Ferguson also figures to sit out the Rams' Week 4 game after spraining his ankle against the Broncos, McVay said. Tight end Colby Parkinson sprained his AC joint in the game, but McVay said his status for the game is still to be determined.

McVay reiterated Monday that he was "hopeful" wide receiver Puka Nacua could play Sunday against the Eagles. Nacua has sat out the past two games because of soreness in his groin.

"It sounds like he had a good workout before the game," McVay said. "We'll continue to see, but if he is able to progress the way that we hope, there's optimism that he'll be able to play this week."

articles.headline: Chargers' Jim Harbaugh on struggling Justin Herbert: 'Be better'
articles.description: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh offered a rare public critique of Justin Herbert on Monday, imploring the quarterback to "be better."
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Los Angeles Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh offered a rare public critique of quarterback Justin Herbert a day after the team's 24-16 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

​"Be better. Be better," Harbaugh said of Herbert's decision-making. "And that drives Justin, that drives me, that drives his position coach, that drives Mike [McDaniel], the coordinator. I mean, drives us all."

Since he took the job in 2023, Harbaugh has avoided criticizing his star quarterback, often willing to point out other players' mistakes in defense of the QB. Harbaugh said Herbert's interception in Week 2 against the Las Vegas Raiders was wide receiver Derius Davis' fault, for example. In Week 1, when two Arizona Cardinals defenders ran free at Herbert for a sack, Harbaugh said Herbert's protection calls weren't an issue; rather, wide receiver Tre' Harris ran the wrong route.

Harbaugh has said throughout his tenure that he thinks Herbert is the greatest quarterback of all time. He once said he wishes he could trade genes with Herbert because of how perfect a player and person he is.

​Last week, Harbaugh said he "wouldn't change a thing about Justin."

​That makes Harbaugh's criticisms Monday all the more meaningful, as Herbert hasn't looked like the player many consider among the NFL's most talented quarterbacks this season.

​Sunday's game marked another poor performance for Herbert, who looks like a shell of himself in McDaniel's offense. Herbert finished with 226 passing yards, one touchdown and an interception, but could have easily had three picks if Bills defenders hadn't dropped two. ​The interception that was caught, by C.J. Gardner-Johnson, was almost thrown directly to the safety. The ball was intended for wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling, but Gardner-Johnson was in coverage, clearly waiting for the ball.

​"Poor awareness, poor decision. Throws him a meatball sub," said Tom Brady, the former quarterback turned color commentator for Fox Sports.

​The offense has been the Chargers' Achilles' heel through three games. General manager Joe Hortiz spent this offseason retooling the offense in McDaniel's vision, a scheme based on anticipatory throwing and wide zone runs. In training camp, McDaniel said Herbert had been significantly ahead of any other quarterbacks he had worked with in their first year in the system, but Herbert has never looked less comfortable through three games.

​The Chargers lost despite the defense forcing five turnovers Sunday, when the offense scored only 14 points. Time and time again, the defense gave the offense an opportunity as the Chargers searched for their first win of the season.

Instead, Herbert and the offense looked as disjointed as they had all year -- drops from tight end Oronde Gadsden and Quentin Johnston, five offensive penalties in the third quarter, and even a missed Cameron Dicker field goal attempt.

articles.headline: Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade
articles.description: Jayson Tatum says he's thankful for his time with Jaylen Brown and the success they shared but feels comfortable leading the new-look Celtics this season.
articles.body:
BOSTON -- Jayson Tatum 's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics has been having Jaylen Brown as a teammate.

That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP - to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship.

"The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during the Celtics media day on Monday. "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years."

The closeness of the Tatum and Brown's off-court relationship -- or lack thereof -- was a topic of conversation throughout their time together as teammates, especially as it became clearer that having two $300 million contracts on the books would be unsustainable for the team's salary cap health going forward.

The choice was ultimately to keep Tatum, sending Brown to an interdivision rival that has suddenly vaulted to a contender in the Eastern Conference after also picking up LeBron James this offseason.

It has cast a brighter spotlight on Tatum, a six-time All-star and five-time All-NBA selection, as the unequivocal leader of the Celtics as he enters his first full season after tearing his Achilles tendon during the 2025 NBA playoffs.

He said he's ready to take on the challenge of leading new-look version of the Celtics, that got back Paul George in the trade and added big man Mitchell Robinson and guard Mike Conley Jr.

"Yeah, very comfortable. This is Year 10," Tatum said. "Leadership is about a lot of different things. Awareness is the biggest one. Self-awareness, awareness of the group. And just understanding we all have roles and we're just kind of simply in this together. So it looks different from person to person."

Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla said the style of the team won't necessarily change without Brown.

"I don't think that it's necessarily the phrase 'without Jaylen,'" Mazzulla said. "Every year you're getting new players, old players, the same players that you have coming back expand their games and they look differently. So it's not as much what it looks like without one person or the other as much as it's what's our roster, how can we take advantage of the strengths and talent that we have."

Tatum describes health as 'great' Tatum reached the 16-month mark since he had surgery on his Achilles tendon and he said he's ready to go after having to miss Game 7 of Boston's first-round playoff matchup against the Sixers last season.

articles.headline: Zion Williamson, on cusp of 8th season, not where he wants to be
articles.description: Zion Williamson smiled politely, but kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player, saying "I'm not where I need to be."
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- Zion Williamson smiled politely, but kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player.

"I'm not where I want to be," Williamson said, nodding in apparent acknowledgement of how little the New Orleans Pelicans have accomplished since drafting the magnetic power forward first overall out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be."

For the eighth time on Monday, the 26-year-old Williamson donned a Pelicans uniform for the franchise's media day. If he's still wearing a jersey when the playoffs start in mid April, it will be a first in his highly lucrative, yet largely unsatisfying NBA career.

Williamson's new coach Jamahl Mosley will be his fifth.

"It's not the way I would have wanted it to be, but that's just part of this business," Williamson said. "All you can do is just adjust with it and hope that things get better."

Williamson has missed 278 career games -- including the entire 2021-22 season -- because of a series of injuries and struggles with fitness. But when he has played, he has averaged nearly 24 points, mixing his uncanny ability to finish through contact in the paint with explosive, above-the-rim highlights.

Now Williamson appears committed, perhaps like never before, to do his part to improve the Pelicans' fortunes. He has reported for training camp in "impeccable condition," according Pelicans basketball operations chief Joe Dumars.

The 6-foot-6 Williamson is listed at 277 pounds, down from 284 -- a figure that had appeared on the club's official roster for the previous seven seasons.

"At some point, you just want the player to get it," said Dumars, now entering his second season with New Orleans. "If someone has to call you every morning to drag you out of bed, to get you to work out, you don't get it yet. But when you're up and you're doing it, and you're the one leading it, then you start looking at that guy and you go, 'Okay, he's good.'

"That's what I saw from him this year," Dumars continued. "You can't play 82 games and not be in great shape. And so we talked about him being in impeccable condition and he has done that."

Dumars said he also spoke with Williamson about becoming more of a leader and diversifying his game, namely by becoming a more consistent and willing jump shooter so that he can punish teams who defend him by collapsing into the paint.

Williamson spent the summer "working with different people, looking at the game different ways, just trying to find different ways to get better," he said. "I've improved with mentally trusting myself and trusting my game, just trusting the work I've put in to the point to where I'm not second-guessing myself."

Williamson summarized his new attitude toward shooting jump shots as: "If I miss, I miss. The next shot's going in."

articles.headline: Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) to make Eagles debut on Monday
articles.description: Edge Jonathan Greenard is set to make his Eagles debut Monday night. He has been sidelines with a pectoral injury he sustained while lifting weights over the summer.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Edge rusher Jonathan Greenard was active for Monday night's game at the Chicago Bears and will make his Philadelphia Eagles debut.

Greenard has been sidelined with a pectoral injury he sustained while lifting weights over the summer. He was listed as questionable on the injury report this week.

While the Eagles will gladly welcome Greenard into the mix, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said last Tuesday that he is "nowhere near ready" for a full workload.

"He's not only coming off inactivity, he's coming off an injury," Fangio said. "His injury for a good bit -- the first, I don't know, four to six, seven weeks -- he really couldn't do a whole lot conditioning-wise either."

Greenard was sidelined for all of training camp and for the first two regular-season games. The Eagles' defense has produced a 45% pressure rate through two games this season, the second-best rate entering Week 3 after the Vikings (48%), but has netted just three sacks, tied for the fifth fewest in the NFL.

Philadelphia acquired Greenard, 29, in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings during draft weekend in April and agreed to a lucrative new deal with the star linebacker.

The Eagles sent two third-round draft picks -- the No. 98 pick in this year's draft and a third-rounder next year -- to the Vikings for Greenard, who then agreed to a four-year, $100 million extension that also includes $50 million in guaranteed money.

Greenard is expected to assume a starting role for the Super Bowl-hopeful Eagles when healthy, leading a group that also includes Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, AJ Epenesa and Arnold Ebiketie.

Greenard had three sacks in 12 games last season after double-digit sack campaigns the previous two years in Minnesota.

He spent the first four years of his career with the Houston Texans before signing a four-year, $72 million deal with the Vikings in 2024. He recorded 12.5 sacks and was named to the Pro Bowl in his first season with the Vikings but was slowed because of a shoulder injury that ultimately required season-ending surgery in 2025.

articles.headline: NFL Week 3's best arrivals, led by Jalen Hurts
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.body:
The official start of fall means it's fit season, when players start dominating the gameday tunnels with eye-popping jackets, sweaters and pants.

Last week, the Philadelphia Eagles played a blazing hot game in Nashville that had players' cleats melting with with temperatures of up to 157 degrees Fahrenheit on the turf. 

Hopefully this week is the start of a heat decline with more cloudier 50-to-75 degree days ahead to allow players to comfortably show off their fits.

To kick off Week 3, Green Bay Packers quarterbacks Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor rocked my two favorite outfits of the Thursday primetime slate.

Love came in shining -- literally -- with a Public School New York x KAY jewelry collaboration jacket: the definition of a statement piece.

Meanwhile, Taylor's Dries Van Noten sweater is the perfect kickoff to fall -- warm but fashion-forward. There are so many fabric design details within this one piece, showing the value of layers.

Here are Week 3 fits that caught our eye:

Monday night fashion

The Philadelphia Eagles and Chicago Bears brought plenty of style to Soldier Field ahead of their "Monday Night Football" matchup. 

Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts pulled off a beige double-breasted suit look that was equal parts fly city jazz singer and CEO of an upstart-turned-Fortune 500 company.

This Week 3 fit is a perfect example of Hurts' signature soulful style that commands respect and translates seamlessly from the tunnel to the field to his postgame presser one-liners.

Sunday's best

For primetime show, it's a who wore it better. The Los Angeles Rams duo of Davante Adams and Byron Young went with all-denim jacket and pant combos. Both can't miss ahead of "Sunday Night Football."

The Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys brought their contrasting styles to Maracanã Stadium for the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro. Lamar Jackson donned a graphic tee paying homage to the late rapper DMX, while George Pickens' fit featured Brazil's national colors in a nod to the host country. 

San Francisco 49ers safety Malik Mustapha styling with an eye-popping Kid Super jacket was my favorite of this window.

From Stefon Diggs' black jacket covered in NBA throwback logo patches, to Malik Nabers' custom "H1M" pendant, players brought plenty of style and personality ahead of the early slate.

Four standouts in this window included Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Donte Jackson 's Boardwalk Vintage fit, which completed a preppy rockstar vibe. Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young KITH x New York to the world jersey was a winner. Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins leaned into the Fall Cleveland vibes with this unique Celine sweater. I love retro call backs so must give Diggs love on his vintage NBA bomber jacket.

Thursday night fashion

The Green Bay Packers host the Atlanta Falcons to kick off Week 3's slate, and quarterback Jordan Love entered the home opener in style, pairing an oversize studded leather pullover with black trousers

articles.descriptionJa: パルマはセリエA開幕5試合でわずか1勝にとどまり、日曜日にカルロス・クエスタ監督と解任・退任の道を歩むこととなった。
